content: 1. Administer 9% sodium chloride (NaCl) intravenously prior to each infusion of cidofovir. This should be infused over 1-2 hours. If tolerated, a second liter of 9% NaCl may be administered over 1-3 hours either at the start of the cidofovir infusion or immediately following it. 2. There is no available data on the efficacy of cidofovir in treating monkeypox in humans. However, cidofovir has demonstrated effectiveness against orthopoxviruses in in vitro and animal studies. 3. The CDC has an expanded access protocol that permits the use of stockpiled cidofovir for the treatment of orthopoxvirus infections, including monkeypox, during an outbreak. 4. Serious renal toxicity or other adverse events have not been observed with brincidofovir (a prodrug of cidofovir) during the treatment of cytomegalovirus infections, in contrast to cidofovir. 5. State and territorial health authorities can request medical countermeasures for monkeypox treatment directly from the CDC Emergency Operations Center at 770-488-7100. 6. The safety and efficacy of cidofovir in individuals under 18 years of age have not been established. 7. The concurrent use of cidofovir with amikacin, amphotericin B deoxycholate, iodinated contrast media, cyclosporine, ioversol, neomycin (oral), tacrolimus, teicoplanin, or other nephrotoxic or ototoxic agents is contraindicated due to the increased risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. These agents should be discontinued at least 7 days prior to initiating cidofovir therapy. 8. The combination of cidofovir with acyclovir, bacitracin, capreomycin, carboplatin, cisplatin, colistin, gentamicin, oxaliplatin, polymyxin B, streptomycin, tenofovir DF, or vancomycin should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used due to the increased risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. If unavoidable, therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 9. The coadministration of cidofovir with deferiprone, dichlorphenamide, elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF, foscarnet, hydroxyurea, ifosfamide, lomustine, methotrexate, methoxyflurane, paromomycin, pentamidine, peramivir, streptozocin, or voclosporin may increase the toxicity of one or both drugs. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored for adverse effects. 10. When cidofovir is coadministered with zidovudine and probenecid, zidovudine clearance may be reduced. The zidovudine dose should be reduced by 50% on days of cidofovir/probenecid administration. 11. The coadministration of cidofovir with acalabrutinib, cabozantinib, or ropeginterferon alfa-2b may increase the risk of myelosuppression or other toxicities. Use caution, monitor closely, and consider alternative therapies if possible. 12. The combination of cidofovir with entecavir may increase the serum concentrations of either drug by reducing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 13. Coadministration of cidofovir with drugs that reduce renal function or compete for active tubular secretion (e.g., emtricitabine, tenofovir, entecavir) may increase serum concentrations of these drugs. Use caution and monitor renal function closely. 14. The concurrent use of cidofovir with drugs associated with neutropenia or agranulocytosis (e.g., deferiprone) should be avoided. If no alternative is available, monitor the absolute neutrophil count more frequently. 15. Cidofovir and dichlorphenamide both decrease serum potassium and may cause metabolic acidosis. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 16. The coadministration of cidofovir with lomustine or methotrexate may enhance the toxicities of myelosuppressive agents. Monitor for increased risk of myelosuppression and adjust therapy as needed. 17. The use of cidofovir with methoxyflurane, paromomycin, or pentamidine may increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 18. Cidofovir increases the levels of peramivir by decreasing renal clearance. Use caution when coadministering peramivir with nephrotoxic drugs. 19. The coadministration of cidofovir with tobramycin (inhaled or systemic) increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid concurrent or sequential use to reduce the risk of ototoxicity. 20. Ublituximab may decrease the effects of cidofovir by immunosuppressive mechanisms, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. The coadministration of cidofovir with zidovudine increases the risk of myelosuppression. Use caution, monitor closely, and consider alternative therapies. 22. The coadministration of cidofovir with voclosporin may increase the risk of acute and/or chronic nephrotoxicity. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored.
